title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: usage reports in the Microsoft Graph API
summary: The briefing's report fields, beta qualification, licensing wording and governance controls are supported by the roadmap and Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections concern a missing reference and the checklist's consent step, which has no corresponding control row.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Graph reporting matching the admin center report, including enabled and active tenant counts and overall and per-app last activity per user.
claims.quote: Metrics included in the Graph API will match those available in the Copilot for Microsoft 365 usage report in the Microsoft 365 admin center, including tenant-level count of enabled users and active users, as well as last activity date per user (all up and per Microsoft 365 app).

claims.claim: The beta reference documents JSON responses.
claims.quote: If successful, this function returns a `200 OK` response code and a JSON representation of the requested report in the response body.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn calls the admin center report the Microsoft Copilot usage report.
claims.quote: # Microsoft Copilot usage report

claims.claim: Microsoft's usage reports overview describes identifying users who might not need a licence.
claims.quote: you can see who uses a service to the fullest extent and who barely uses it and might not need a Microsoft 365 license.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Tenant administrator consent is required for application-level and delegated application access.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Entra tenant administrator must explicitly grant consent to your application. This is required both for application-level authorization and user delegated authorization.

claims.claim: Delegated reporting access requires a limited administrator role from the authorization page's stated list.
claims.quote: Company Administrator, Exchange Administrator, SharePoint Administrator, Lync Administrator, Teams Service Administrator, Teams Communications Administrator, Global Reader, Usage Summary Reports Reader, or Reports Reader.

claims.claim: The Copilot user detail reference additionally lists AI Administrator.
claims.quote:
the tenant administrator must assign the user one of the following Microsoft Entra ID limited administrator roles:

- Company Administrator
- AI Administrator

claims.claim: Global Reader and Usage Summary Reports Reader have tenant-level access without detailed metrics.
claims.quote: The Global Reader and Usage Summary Reports Reader roles will only have access to tenant-level data, without visibility into detailed metrics.

claims.claim: Application-level authorization can read usage reports without a signed-in user, and depends on application permissions rather than a delegated user's role.
claims.quote: Application-level authorization - Allows an app to read all service usage reports without a signed-in user. The permissions granted to the application determine authorization.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes reports data as sensitive.
claims.quote: Reports data that is accessible via the Microsoft Graph reports API is sensitive.

claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI

claims.quote: Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The overview lists usage reports among Copilot APIs and requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence per user accessing Copilot functionality via those APIs, supporting the per-user model.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot license - Required for each user who accesses Microsoft 365 Copilot functionality via these APIs. This license provides access to the AI capabilities that power the APIs.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The overview does not explicitly say whether the reporting app or calling administrator itself needs a Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot usage reports" "license" "administrator"; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot "usage reports" "license". Opened Copilot APIs overview, usage user detail and reportroot-authorization; no explicit reports-caller licence rule.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate price, meter or credit rate for these reporting endpoints is published in the cited references and overview.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot usage reports API" "price" "meter". Read Copilot APIs overview and all four reporting function references; none names a reporting-endpoint price or meter. Search results describe Retrieval API and agent meters, not these reporting endpoints.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no separate switch to turn off only the Copilot usage reports API.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "reports" "API" "disable"; "Copilot usage reports" "disable" tenant switch. Read reportroot-authorization, adminReportSettings update and copilotReportRoot references; found consent, roles and concealment, not a feature-specific off switch.

claims.claim: The older beta reference gives no retirement date.
claims.quote: Searched: "getMicrosoft365CopilotUsageUserDetail" "retired"; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/reportroot-getmicrosoft365copilotusageuserdetail retirement deprecation. Read the older beta reference and its migration note; no retirement date is stated.

claims.claim: The admin center report route is Reports > Usage > Reports > Microsoft Copilot > Copilot > Usage.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Reports. ... Select Usage. ... On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Copilot. ... On the report page, select the Usage tab

claims.claim: If Reports is hidden, select Show all before Reports.
claims.quote: If you don't see Reports, select Show all, and then select Reports.

claims.claim: Enabled Users counts unique users with Microsoft Copilot licences during the selected timeframe.
claims.quote: Enabled Users shows the total number of unique users in your organization with Microsoft Copilot licenses over the selected timeframe.

claims.claim: A delegated user's reporting role can be assigned at Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > Users > All users > user > Assigned roles > Add assignment.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center. ... Expand the Identity menu > Users > select All users. ... Select the user. ... Choose Assigned roles, and then Add assignment.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments creates the user's Microsoft Entra role assignment.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

claims.claim: The role assignment request uses roleDefinitionId for the role and principalId for the recipient.
claims.quote: principalId | String | Required. Identifier of the principal to which the assignment is granted. ... roleDefinitionId | String | Identifier of the unifiedRoleDefinition the assignment is for.

claims.claim: The concealment control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/admin/reportSettings updates the tenant's report concealment setting.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings

claims.claim: The request body property displayConcealedNames set to true conceals names.
claims.quote: displayConcealedNames | Boolean | If set to `true`, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If `false`, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: Updating report settings requires ReportSettings.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote:

| Application | ReportSettings.ReadWrite.All | Not available. |
